text: Bayesian posterior-draw estimators, audit_sbc() draws θ̃∼p(θ)\tilde\theta \sim p(\theta), simulates ỹ∼p(y∣θ̃)\tilde y \sim p(y \mid \tilde\theta), computes rank statistics θ̃\tilde\theta among LL posterior draws, tests rank uniformity via Pearson’s χ2\chi^2 Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests:
code: # Exact Normal-Normal conjugate posterior (calibrated) sbc_ok <- audit_sbc(   prior = function() c(mu = rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 2)),   dgp = function(theta) rnorm(20, mean = theta[["mu"]], sd = 1),   posterior_draws = function(y) {     post_var <- 1 / (1 / 4 + length(y))     post_mean <- post_var * sum(y)     rnorm(99, mean = post_mean, sd = sqrt(post_var))   },   n_sim = 100L,   n_bins = 10L,   seed = 42L ) sbc_ok #> [WARN] Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC): 100/100 reps, L = 99 draws, 10 bins #> [WARN] mu: chi2 p = 0.9357, KS p = 0.7920, 50% cov = 47.0%, 90% cov = 80.0%  # Miscalibrated posterior with systematic shift and underdispersion sbc_bad <- audit_sbc(   prior = function() c(mu = rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 2)),   dgp = function(theta) rnorm(20, mean = theta[["mu"]], sd = 1),   posterior_draws = function(y) {     post_var <- 1 / (1 / 4 + length(y))     post_mean <- post_var * sum(y) + 0.5     rnorm(99, mean = post_mean, sd = 0.3 * sqrt(post_var))   },   n_sim = 100L,   n_bins = 10L,   seed = 42L ) sbc_bad #> [FAIL] Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC): 100/100 reps, L = 99 draws, 10 bins #> [FAIL] mu: chi2 p = 0.0000, KS p = 0.0000, 50% cov = 2.0%, 90% cov = 9.0%

what: 2. Linting R Scripts and Quarto Documents
title: Getting Started with statci: Statistical Linting, Manuscript Auditing & CI Reports
text: Unlike style linters, stat_lint() parses full R syntax trees via xmlparsedata xml2. Let’s inspect small analysis script several silent methodological flaws: Notice statci pinpoints distinct statistical hazard—hardcoded personal paths, unseeded stochasticity, preprocessing data splitting, uncentered multilevel interactions, missing convergence/singularity checks, unadjusted multiple testing, mutable F instead FALSE—exact line column coordinates.
code: flawed_script <- ' df <- read.csv("/Users/researcher/Desktop/study.csv") df$x <- scale(df$x) idx <- sample(nrow(df), 80) train <- df[idx, ]  fit <- lme4::lmer(y ~ x * w + (1 + x | school), data = train) pvals <- sapply(1:10, function(j) t.test(rnorm(20), rnorm(20), var.equal = F)$p.value) '  lint_bad <- stat_lint_text(flawed_script) lint_bad #> [FAIL] statci lint: 1 file(s), 20 rule(s) | 2 error(s), 5 warning(s), 0 info #> WARN  <text:r>:2:16 (absolute_path_in_script): Hardcoded non-portable path #> "/Users/researcher/Desktop/study.csv" inside `read.csv()` breaks #> CI/reproducibility; use project-relative paths (e.g., `file.path()` or #> `here::here()`). #> ERROR <text:r>:3:9 (preprocessing_before_split): Potential train/test data #> leakage: `scale()` is applied before data splitting on the full dataset; fit #> preprocessing parameters on training data only. #> ERROR <text:r>:4:8 (unseeded_randomness): Stochastic call `sample()` invoked #> without a preceding `set.seed()` or `withr::with_seed()` call. #> WARN  <text:r>:7:8 (missing_convergence_check): `lmer()` fitted without checking #> `lme4::isSingular()` or `@optinfo$conv`; boundary/singular fits or optimizer #> non-convergence may go undetected. #> WARN  <text:r>:7:8 (uncentered_mlm_interaction): Multilevel interaction in #> `lmer()` uses uncentered predictor(s): `w`. Center Level-1/Level-2 predictors #> (e.g., cluster-mean or grand-mean centering) to prevent contextual confounding #> and aid interpretation. #> WARN  <text:r>:8:10 (unadjusted_multiple_testing): Repeated hypothesis testing #> inside `sapply()` without `p.adjust()` or multiple-testing correction in scope. #> WARN  <text:r>:8:76 (short_logical_literal): Mutable symbol `F` used instead of #> `FALSE`. `T`/`F` can be overwritten by variables and silently corrupt #> statistical arguments.

title: Multiverse Specification Curves, Incremental PR Diff Linting & New AST Rules
text: audit_multiverse() evaluates user-supplied modeling pipeline across full Cartesian grid analytical decision forks, returning specification-level estimates, confidence intervals, p-values, sign consistency, median interquartile range (IQR), per-fork variance decomposition (eta_squared) pinpoints decision fork drives estimate dispersion.

title: Multiverse Specification Curves, Incremental PR Diff Linting & New AST Rules
text: First, simulate clean dataset x strong, genuine linear relationship y regardless reasonable analytical choices: Every specification agrees direction (sign_consistency = 100%) statistical significance (p <= 0.05 across 12 specifications), tight IQR dispersion. can visualize sorted specification curve underlying decision matrix directly via plot():
code: set.seed(2026) n <- 120L study_df <- data.frame(   x = rnorm(n),   age = rnorm(n),   ses = rnorm(n) ) study_df$y <- 1.5 + 0.85 * study_df$x + 0.25 * study_df$age - 0.15 * study_df$ses + rnorm(n, sd = 0.6)  decisions <- list(   outliers = c("none", "winsor_5pct"),   covariates = c("bivariate", "age_only", "age_and_ses"),   transform = c("raw", "centered") )  fit_spec <- function(d, spec) {   if (spec$outliers == "winsor_5pct") {     qs <- stats::quantile(d$y, c(0.05, 0.95))     d$y <- pmin(pmax(d$y, qs[1L]), qs[2L])   }   if (spec$transform == "centered") {     d$x <- d$x - mean(d$x)   }   fml <- switch(     spec$covariates,     bivariate = y ~ x,     age_only = y ~ x + age,     age_and_ses = y ~ x + age + ses   )   stats::lm(fml, data = d) }  mv_robust <- audit_multiverse(   data = study_df,   decisions = decisions,   fit_fn = fit_spec,   param = "x" )  summary(mv_robust) #> [PASS] statci Multiverse Specification Curve (x: 12/12 valid specs) #> median = 0.7953, IQR = 0.0518 [min = 0.7686, max = 0.8224] #> sign consistency = 100.0%, p <= 0.05 = 100.0%, top driver = outliers #> Decision Fork Variance Decomposition: #> - outliers (2 levels): median range = 0.0518, eta^2 = 99.8% #> - covariates (3 levels): median range = 0.0023, eta^2 = 0.2% #> - transform (2 levels): median range = 0.0000, eta^2 = 0.0% plot(mv_robust)

what: Catching Analytical Fragility and Pinpointing Its Driver
title: Multiverse Specification Curves, Incremental PR Diff Linting & New AST Rules
text: Now introduce single extreme leverage outlier dataset whose true underlying slope negative. Without winsorization, OLS flips sign; 5% winsorization, true negative slope recovered: audit_multiverse() automatically flags status = "fail", reports sign_consistency = 50%, ranks outliers top variance driver (eta_squared near 100%).  can also extract full specification table as_tibble() embed multiverse = mv_robust directly statci_report() alongside lint, calibration, manuscript, sensitivity checks:
code: fragile_df <- study_df fragile_df$y <- -0.40 * fragile_df$x + 0.20 * fragile_df$age + rnorm(n, sd = 0.35) fragile_df$x[1L] <- 15 fragile_df$y[1L] <- 28  mv_fragile <- audit_multiverse(   data = fragile_df,   decisions = list(     outliers = c("keep_all", "winsor_5pct"),     covariates = c("bivariate", "age_only", "age_and_ses")   ),   fit_fn = function(d, spec) {     if (spec$outliers == "winsor_5pct") {       qx <- stats::quantile(d$x, c(0.05, 0.95))       qy <- stats::quantile(d$y, c(0.05, 0.95))       d$x <- pmin(pmax(d$x, qx[1L]), qx[2L])       d$y <- pmin(pmax(d$y, qy[1L]), qy[2L])     }     fml <- switch(       spec$covariates,       bivariate = y ~ x,       age_only = y ~ x + age,       age_and_ses = y ~ x + age + ses     )     stats::lm(fml, data = d)   },   param = "x" )  summary(mv_fragile) #> [FAIL] statci Multiverse Specification Curve (x: 6/6 valid specs) #> median = 0.3203, IQR = 1.4025 [min = -0.3843, max = 1.0486] #> sign consistency = 50.0%, p <= 0.05 = 100.0%, top driver = outliers #> Decision Fork Variance Decomposition: #> - outliers (2 levels): median range = 1.4036, eta^2 = 100.0% #> - covariates (3 levels): median range = 0.0169, eta^2 = 0.0% plot(mv_fragile) head(as_tibble(mv_robust)[, c("spec_id", "outliers", "covariates", "estimate", "p_value", "significant")]) #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   spec_id outliers    covariates  estimate  p_value significant #>     <int> <chr>       <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl> <lgl>       #> 1       4 winsor_5pct age_only       0.769 1.48e-24 TRUE        #> 2      10 winsor_5pct age_only       0.769 1.48e-24 TRUE        #> 3       2 winsor_5pct bivariate      0.770 7.72e-24 TRUE        #> 4       8 winsor_5pct bivariate      0.770 7.72e-24 TRUE        #> 5       6 winsor_5pct age_and_ses    0.771 1.13e-24 TRUE        #> 6      12 winsor_5pct age_and_ses    0.771 1.13e-24 TRUE  rep <- statci_report(multiverse = mv_robust, title = "Multiverse Verification Audit") rep #> [PASS] Multiverse Verification Audit #> [PASS] Multiverse Specification Curve: 12/12 specs; median = 0.795, IQR = #> 0.052, sign consistency = 100.0%

text: CI pipelines air-gapped environments, can pass unified diff string directly via diff_text: Notice two crucial properties: Line 1 (legacy_draw <- rnorm(100)) untouched PR, suppressed (n_suppressed_untouched = 1) rather blocking PR. Line 3 (fresh_draw <- rnorm(50)) falsely flagged unseeded stat_lint_diff() parses full file AST sees set.seed(2026) line 2. Line 4 (bad_flag <- mean(fresh_draw) == 0.5) caught equality_on_float.

Use `isTRUE(all.equal(...))` or #> `abs(a - b) < tol` instead. diff_res$diff_meta$n_suppressed_untouched #> [1] 1

what: 3. Silent Data-Integrity AST Rules (20 Built-In Rules)
title: Multiverse Specification Curves, Incremental PR Diff Linting & New AST Rules
text: statci ships 20 built-AST lint rules. Three high-impact data-integrity rules catch silent statistical bugs never raise R errors: unverified_merge_cardinality: Flags dplyr::left_join(), inner_join(), full_join(), right_join(), base merge() calls neither declare relationship = ... verify nrow() /joining, protecting silent many--many row duplication inflates sample sizes shrinks standard errors. missing_drop_false_matrix: Flags 2D matrix/array subsetting X[, cols] X[idx, ] lacking drop = FALSE, silently collapses 1-row 1-column subsets atomic vectors breaks downstream matrix algebra (%*%, solve(), crossprod()). implicit_na_rm_masking: Flags unconditional na.rm = TRUE inside statistical summaries (mean(), sd(), var(), sum(), median(), quantile(), min(), max()) without nearby missingness inspection (.na(), anyNA(), complete.cases(), na.omit(), drop_na()). explicitly guard join cardinality, preserve matrix dimensions drop = FALSE, audit missingness summarizing, 20 built-rules pass cleanly:
code: subtle_code <- ' set.seed(2026) joined <- merge(patients, visits, by = "id") X_sub <- design_mat[, selected_cols] avg_score <- mean(joined$score, na.rm = TRUE) '  stat_lint_text(   subtle_code,   rules = c(     "unverified_merge_cardinality",     "missing_drop_false_matrix",     "implicit_na_rm_masking"   ) ) #> [WARN] statci lint: 1 file(s), 3 rule(s) | 0 error(s), 2 warning(s), 0 info #> WARN  <text:r>:3:11 (unverified_merge_cardinality): `merge()` called without #> `relationship =` or a post-merge row-count assertion (`nrow()` / #> `stopifnot()`); unintended duplicate keys can silently multiply rows. #> WARN  <text:r>:5:14 (implicit_na_rm_masking): `mean(..., na.rm = TRUE)` silently #> discards missing values with no `is.na()` / `anyNA()` / `complete.cases()` #> missingness check or report in scope. guarded_code <- ' set.seed(2026) n_before <- nrow(patients) joined <- merge(patients, visits, by = "id") stopifnot(identical(nrow(joined), n_before)) X_sub <- design_mat[, selected_cols, drop = FALSE] n_missing <- sum(is.na(joined$score)) avg_score <- mean(joined$score, na.rm = TRUE) '  stat_lint_text(guarded_code) #> [PASS] statci lint: 1 file(s), 20 rule(s) | 0 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info

what: Audit posterior calibration via Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) — audit_sbc
title: Audit posterior calibration via Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) — audit_sbc
text: Implements Simulation-Based Calibration (Talts et al., 2018) Bayesian posterior-sampling estimators. Repeatedly draws true parameters \(\tilde{\theta} \sim p(\theta)\), simulates synthetic data \(\tilde{y} \sim p(y \mid \tilde{\theta})\), draws \(L\) posterior samples, evaluates uniformity rank statistics via Pearson's chi-square test Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, together empirical 50% 90% central credible-interval coverage.
